name: Legal
summary: After-hours lead recovery, intake, deadlines, case status updates, and billing.

automations.title: Matter Profitability & Unbilled Time Alert System
automations.summary: At the end of each week, this automation pulls every open matter the attorney has billed time to, compares total time captured against the retainer…
steps: At the end of each week, this automation pulls every open matter the attorney has billed time to, compares total time captured against the retainer balance or budget estimate, and delivers a per-matter profitability summary.

Matters where time captured is tracking to exceed the budget by more than 20% receive an immediate flag so the attorney can have a scope conversation with the client before the overage becomes an invoice dispute.
Unbilled time sitting more than 10 days without being applied to an invoice triggers a reminder, because time that isn't captured quickly is time that disappears permanently.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on an attorney remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Practice management/billing software (e.g., Clio or TimeSolv)

automations.title: Discovery Request Tracker & Response Deadline System
automations.summary: When a discovery request is received and logged, this automation calculates the response deadline based on the applicable rules (federal, state, or…
steps: When a discovery request is received and logged, this automation calculates the response deadline based on the applicable rules (federal, state, or local) creates a series of internal preparation deadlines working backward from that date, and assigns tasks to the responsible attorney and paralegal with escalating reminders.
Any task that misses its internal deadline triggers an immediate flag to the supervising attorney.
Litigation is managed to a calendar, not to whoever remembered to check their inbox that morning.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a paralegal has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Vendor Invoice Approval & Payment Scheduling System
automations.summary: Every vendor invoice received by the firm (court reporter, process server, expert witness, office supplies) is automatically routed to the…
steps: Every vendor invoice received by the firm (court reporter, process server, expert witness, office supplies) is automatically routed to the appropriate matter or overhead code, sent to the office manager for one-click approval, and queued for payment on the next scheduled payment run.
Invoices that sit unapproved for more than five business days trigger an escalation.

At month end, an expense summary by matter and by vendor category is generated automatically, giving the office manager the data needed for budget reviews without exporting anything manually from any system.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a law firm office manager re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: QuickBooks Online or a legal billing platform
Jotform or email (invoice intake and approval flow)

automations.title: Missed Call & After-Hours Lead Recovery System
automations.summary: Every missed call to the firm's main line triggers an automatic text back to the caller within two minutes, acknowledging the call and asking what…
steps: Every missed call to the firm's main line triggers an automatic text back to the caller within two minutes, acknowledging the call and asking what they're calling about, converting a missed call into a text conversation the intake specialist can respond to when available.
Calls and web form submissions that come in after hours are logged, auto-acknowledged with a clear response time expectation, and added to the intake specialist's morning queue with full context.
Firms that adopt this system stop losing prospective clients to competitors who answered first, because the firm's first response now goes out in seconds regardless of the hour.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a legal intake specialist re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Phone system with missed call webhook (e.g., RingCentral or Grasshopper)

automations.title: Referral Partner Tracking & Nurture System
automations.summary: Every time a new client lists a referral source during intake, the system logs the referring attorney, accountant, or business contact, updates…
steps: Every time a new client lists a referral source during intake, the system logs the referring attorney, accountant, or business contact, updates their referral count in the CRM, and automatically triggers a personalized thank-you email from the firm.

Referral partners who haven't sent a case in 90 days receive a gentle check-in from the marketing manager, turning the referral network from a mental note into a systematically managed revenue channel.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a legal marketing manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Consultation Scheduling & Qualification Bot
automations.summary: When a prospective client fills out the contact form or texts the firm's main number, this automation runs them through a short qualifying sequence…
steps: When a prospective client fills out the contact form or texts the firm's main number, this automation runs them through a short qualifying sequence: practice area, case type, jurisdiction, and rough timeline.
Inquiries that fall outside the firm's practice areas or licensed jurisdictions are automatically filtered out with a polite referral message instead of landing in an attorney's inbox.

Qualified leads are routed to the correct attorney's calendar based on practice area and booked directly into an open consultation slot, with a confirmation text and calendar invite sent within seconds.
The managing partner gets a daily summary of every inquiry, qualified or not, so nothing falls through the cracks and no attorney wastes a 30-minute slot on a case the firm was never going to take.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a managing partner has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

automations.title: Case Status Update Text System
automations.summary: As a matter moves through its key stages, filing, discovery, mediation, settlement, or a trial date being set, this automation fires a…
steps: As a matter moves through its key stages, filing, discovery, mediation, settlement, or a trial date being set, this automation fires a plain-language status update text to the client the moment the matter's status field changes in the practice management system.
Each update is pulled from a pre-approved template library so the language stays consistent and nothing client-facing goes out without review.
Clients can reply with a quick question that gets routed straight to the client relations coordinator instead of leaving a voicemail that takes two days to return.
Firms running this typically see "any updates?" calls drop by more than half, because clients stop feeling like they have to call just to find out their case still exists.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a client relations coordinator handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Document Request Follow-Up System
automations.summary: When a client is asked for documents, whether it's financial records for a divorce, medical bills for a personal injury claim, or signed affidavits…
steps: When a client is asked for documents, whether it's financial records for a divorce, medical bills for a personal injury claim, or signed affidavits, this automation logs the outstanding request and starts a follow-up sequence: a reminder text at 72 hours, a second reminder with a direct secure upload link at 5 days, and an escalation to the litigation support specialist for a personal call at 8 days if nothing has arrived.
Every uploaded document is automatically matched to the open request and marked complete, so staff spend no time cross-checking what's been received against what's still owed.
Firms typically cut the average time to collect a full document set by several days simply by removing the guesswork of who's still waiting on what.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a litigation support specialist spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)
Secure client portal (e.g., Clio's client portal or NetDocuments)

automations.title: E-Signature Follow-Up Automation
automations.summary: Once an engagement letter or other document is sent out for signature, this automation tracks its status in real time and automatically sends a…
steps: Once an engagement letter or other document is sent out for signature, this automation tracks its status in real time and automatically sends a reminder email at 48 hours and a reminder text at 96 hours if it's still unsigned.

Documents that remain unsigned after 7 days trigger a task for the client onboarding coordinator to reach out personally, since a matter can't officially open, and billing can't officially start, until the engagement letter is signed.
Every reminder pulls the client's name and document title automatically, so nothing goes out generic or gets sent to the wrong person.
Engagement letters that used to sit unsigned for a week or more now typically close out within a day or two of the first reminder.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a client onboarding coordinator has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Missed Call Text-Back System
automations.summary: Every call that rings through to voicemail, whether the attorney is in court, in a deposition, or simply on another line, triggers an automatic text…
steps: Every call that rings through to voicemail, whether the attorney is in court, in a deposition, or simply on another line, triggers an automatic text within 60 seconds thanking the caller and asking two quick questions: what kind of legal matter it's regarding and the best time to reach them back.

The caller's reply is captured automatically as a new lead card with their answers already filled in, so the attorney opens a ready-to-call list instead of a string of unlabeled voicemails at the end of the day.
For a solo or small practice without a receptionist covering every line, this alone recovers callers who would otherwise hang up and call the next firm on their search results.
Practices using this typically convert a meaningfully higher share of missed calls into booked consultations simply because someone, or something, answered within a minute.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a solo practice attorney has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Phone system with missed call webhook (e.g., RingCentral or Grasshopper)

automations.title: Client Intake to CRM Sync System
automations.summary: When a new client submits the firm's web intake form, this automation instantly creates a matching record in the CRM with their contact information…
steps: When a new client submits the firm's web intake form, this automation instantly creates a matching record in the CRM with their contact information, case type, referral source, and a preliminary conflict-check flag based on opposing party names entered on the form.

The new client coordinator receives a notification the moment a submission needs manual conflict review, while clean submissions move straight into the assigned attorney's queue with no re-typing required.
Every field maps automatically from the web form to the CRM, so what a prospective client types once is the same data the firm works from through the entire matter.
Firms using this eliminate the lag, and the transcription errors, that come from an intake specialist retyping form submissions into the CRM by hand.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a new client coordinator, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Web form tool (e.g., Jotform or Gravity Forms)

automations.title: Review & Testimonial Request System
automations.summary: This automation checks the practice management system daily for matters that have moved to closed status, and once a matter closes, it waits 10 days…
steps: This automation checks the practice management system daily for matters that have moved to closed status, and once a matter closes, it waits 10 days before sending the client a review request, timed specifically to avoid soliciting feedback on a matter that's still pending, which several state bar advertising rules treat as a compliance risk.
The request avoids referencing any case specifics or outcome details and instead asks the client to speak generally to their experience working with the firm.

Positive responses are routed to a public review link for Google or Avvo, while any lower-rated response is routed privately to the client success manager for direct follow-up instead of appearing publicly.
Firms using this build a steady stream of public reviews without ever risking a bar complaint over premature or case-specific solicitation.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a client success manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)
Podium or BirdEye (review routing and publishing)

automations.title: Consultation Request Triage & Routing System
automations.summary: When a prospective client submits a consultation request through the firm's website form in Jotform, the automation reads the practice area field…
steps: When a prospective client submits a consultation request through the firm's website form in Jotform, the automation reads the practice area field and instantly routes the request to the correct attorney or paralegal queue in Clio Grow, tagging urgent matters like an eviction with a hearing date or an upcoming arraignment for same-day callback.

A Zapier workflow starts an internal countdown the moment the request lands, and if no one has logged a response within the firm's target window, it automatically escalates with a Slack alert to the intake coordinator and, if still unanswered, to the managing partner.
Every request and response time logs to a running Google Sheets dashboard so leadership can see exactly where bottlenecks happen.
Firms running this catch same-day, high-urgency matters that used to sit in a shared inbox until someone happened to check it, and average response time typically drops from hours to minutes.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, an intake coordinator spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Client Intake Document Automation
automations.summary: The moment a consultation is booked on Calendly, a Zapier workflow automatically sends the client a secure intake questionnaire through Jotform…
steps: The moment a consultation is booked on Calendly, a Zapier workflow automatically sends the client a secure intake questionnaire through Jotform along with a personalized checklist of required documents, from photo ID to insurance declarations pages, based on the practice area selected at booking.

Completed responses and uploaded files sync directly into the client's matter file in Clio, so the case manager can confirm everything is in before the first meeting instead of chasing paperwork afterward.

Clients who haven't completed the questionnaire 48 hours before their appointment automatically receive a reminder text through Twilio, and anything still outstanding the morning of triggers an internal Slack alert to the case manager.
Attorneys walk into first meetings with signed intake forms, ID copies, and supporting documents already reviewed, cutting roughly 20 minutes of paperwork chasing out of every new matter.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a case manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Automated Case Status Update Notifications
automations.summary: Every time a case's status field changes inside the practice management system, whether it moves from "filed" to "discovery" or "in negotiation" to…
steps: Every time a case's status field changes inside the practice management system, whether it moves from "filed" to "discovery" or "in negotiation" to "settled," the automation automatically translates the internal status code into a plain-language update and pushes it to the client through the Clio client portal and a follow-up email.

A Zapier integration watches for status-field changes in MyCase and fires the notification within minutes rather than waiting for a staff member to remember to update the client, and clients can opt into SMS delivery through Twilio for faster visibility on their phone.

Because clients can see progress in real time instead of wondering, the client services associate's inbound "what's happening with my case" calls typically drop by more than half, freeing several hours a week that used to go to status-check phone calls.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a client services associate re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)
Secure client portal (e.g., Clio's client portal)

automations.title: Engagement Letter E-Signature Reminder Chain
automations.summary: Once an engagement letter or other document is sent for signature through DocuSign, the automation automatically starts a reminder countdown: any…
steps: Once an engagement letter or other document is sent for signature through DocuSign, the automation automatically starts a reminder countdown: any document still unsigned by day 1 triggers a friendly email nudge, day 3 adds a text reminder through Twilio, and day 7 escalates to a phone call task assigned directly to the legal assistant in Clio.

Each reminder pulls the client's name and document title automatically so nothing reads as a generic template, and the moment the document is signed, the sequence cancels itself and the matter automatically moves to the next intake stage in the practice management system.

Legal assistants who used to track pending signatures in a spreadsheet and manually follow up now recover documents days faster on average, and engagement letters rarely sit unsigned for more than a week.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a legal assistant is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background.

automations.title: Statute of Limitations & Deadline Alert System
automations.summary: As soon as a key date, whether a statute of limitations, a filing deadline, or a response due date, is entered into the case management system for a…
steps: As soon as a key date, whether a statute of limitations, a filing deadline, or a response due date, is entered into the case management system for a matter, the automation automatically cross-references it against the firm's docketing calendar in Clio and schedules a chain of advance warnings at 30, 14, 7, and 1 day out.

Alerts go simultaneously to the assigned attorney and the docketing clerk through both email and a shared Google Calendar entry, and any deadline within 48 hours that hasn't been marked complete triggers an urgent Slack alert to the managing partner as a backstop.

Because the system never forgets a date the way an overloaded calendar sometimes does, firms running this build a second layer of protection against the single costliest mistake a firm can make: missing a filing deadline or letting a statute run.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a docketing clerk re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Missed Call Text-Back System
automations.summary: When an inbound call to the firm goes unanswered because every line is busy or it's after hours, the phone system automatically fires a webhook that…
steps: When an inbound call to the firm goes unanswered because every line is busy or it's after hours, the phone system automatically fires a webhook that triggers a Zapier workflow to send the caller a text message within seconds through Twilio, apologizing for missing the call and offering a Calendly link to book a consultation directly.

The text also gives callers the option to reply with their legal issue in a few words, which automatically creates a lead record in Clio Grow tagged by practice area for the intake team to review first thing.
The receptionist gets a morning Slack digest of every missed call and how each one was handled overnight.

Firms running this recover leads that would otherwise call a competitor while waiting on hold, and it's common to convert 15 to 20 percent of missed calls into booked consultations that never would have called back.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a receptionist is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Phone system with missed call webhook (e.g., RingCentral or Grasshopper)

automations.title: Post-Case-Closure Review Request Automation
automations.summary: Once a matter is marked closed and successfully resolved in Clio, the automation automatically waits a set number of days, timed to when client…
steps: Once a matter is marked closed and successfully resolved in Clio, the automation automatically waits a set number of days, timed to when client satisfaction is highest, before sending a review request by email and text through Twilio.
The request links directly to the firm's Google or Avvo review page and avoids referencing any case-specific outcome details to stay within bar advertising guidelines.

Responses are automatically filtered: clients who indicate a positive experience get routed straight to the public review link, while anyone who signals frustration is routed privately to the marketing coordinator for a follow-up call instead of a public post.
Every request and outcome logs to a Google Sheets tracker so the firm can measure response rates over time.
Firms running this consistently see review volume roughly triple compared to relying on staff to remember to ask.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a marketing coordinator has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Referral Source ROI Reporting System
automations.summary: The moment a new client signs an engagement letter, the automation automatically tags their matter in Clio Grow with the originating marketing…
steps: The moment a new client signs an engagement letter, the automation automatically tags their matter in Clio Grow with the originating marketing channel or referral source, whether that's a Google Ads campaign, a referring attorney, or a past client, pulled from the original intake form data captured in Jotform.

A Zapier workflow feeds every tagged signing into a live Google Sheets or Airtable dashboard that calculates signed-client volume and revenue by source automatically, updating in real time rather than requiring someone to compile numbers at month end.

The business development director receives a weekly Slack summary showing which referral sources and marketing channels are actually converting into paying clients versus which ones just generate consultations that go nowhere.
With real signed-revenue attribution instead of a gut feeling, firms typically redirect marketing spend within a quarter toward the two or three sources actually producing business.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a business development director manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Retainer Balance Low Alert System
automations.summary: The automation continuously monitors each client's trust or retainer balance inside the billing platform, and the moment a balance drops below a…
steps: The automation continuously monitors each client's trust or retainer balance inside the billing platform, and the moment a balance drops below a firm-defined threshold, it automatically notifies both the billing coordinator and the client simultaneously: the client through a plain-language email explaining the balance and a secure link to replenish it, and the billing coordinator through a Slack alert flagging the account for follow-up if the client hasn't responded within a few days.

Because the notification is automatic and consistent for every client, no one on staff has to initiate the sometimes-awkward conversation about needing more money, and clients get advance notice before their balance hits zero and work has to pause.
Firms running this see far fewer stalled matters caused by a depleted retainer, and billing staff report the low-balance conversation becoming a non-issue instead of a recurring friction point.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a billing coordinator remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Webinar Signup to Nurture Sequence Automation
automations.summary: Anyone who registers for a free legal webinar or seminar through the firm's registration page in Jotform is automatically added to a topic-specific…
steps: Anyone who registers for a free legal webinar or seminar through the firm's registration page in Jotform is automatically added to a topic-specific nurture sequence in ActiveCampaign the moment they sign up, no manual list-building required.

Attendees who actually show up receive a different follow-up track than no-shows, including a replay link and a related case-study email, while no-shows get a shorter re-engagement sequence with a lighter offer to book a consultation.
A Zapier workflow syncs every registrant into Clio Grow as a tagged lead so the events and marketing coordinator can see webinar-sourced leads separately from other channels.

Prospects who aren't ready to hire an attorney the day of the webinar stay warm through months of relevant content instead of falling off the radar, and firms typically see a meaningful share of webinar attendees convert to consultations weeks or months later.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means an events & marketing coordinator handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Court Date & Hearing Reminder Automation
automations.summary: As soon as a hearing or court date is entered into the case management system, the automation automatically schedules a reminder sequence to both…
steps: As soon as a hearing or court date is entered into the case management system, the automation automatically schedules a reminder sequence to both the client and the assigned trial paralegal at two weeks, three days, and the morning of the appearance, delivered by email and text through Twilio.

Each reminder automatically pulls in the specific logistics for that hearing, courtroom number, judge's name, parking instructions, and a note on what documents or evidence to bring, so nothing has to be typed manually every time.
If a court date changes in Clio, the entire reminder chain automatically reschedules itself rather than requiring staff to catch and manually update it.
Clients show up prepared and on time far more consistently, and the trial paralegal is freed from manually tracking and re-sending reminders for every hearing on the firm's docket each week.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a trial paralegal has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Legal Document Expiration Tracking System
automations.summary: Key documents with hard expiration dates, powers of attorney, business licenses, professional permits, and similar filings, are automatically logged…
steps: Key documents with hard expiration dates, powers of attorney, business licenses, professional permits, and similar filings, are automatically logged into a tracking system the moment they're entered into Clio, and the automation calculates renewal deadlines and schedules advance alerts at 90, 30, and 7 days out.

Both the client and the compliance paralegal receive the alerts: the client through email with plain-language renewal instructions, and the paralegal through a Slack notification tied to a task in the practice management system.
A running Airtable dashboard shows every tracked document across the firm's entire client base sorted by days remaining, so nothing depends on one person's memory.

Because renewals surface automatically well ahead of the deadline instead of when a client suddenly realizes their permit lapsed, firms catch expirations weeks in advance and avoid the scramble that comes with a document lapsing unnoticed.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a compliance paralegal, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Monthly Billing Invoice Auto-Generation
automations.summary: Throughout the month, as attorneys log billable time entries directly in Clio or TimeSolv, the automation automatically compiles every entry tied to…
steps: Throughout the month, as attorneys log billable time entries directly in Clio or TimeSolv, the automation automatically compiles every entry tied to a matter into a draft invoice on a set billing cycle rather than waiting for someone to manually pull time records at month end.

Draft invoices route automatically to the billing manager in QuickBooks Online for a final review, with any entry missing a description or exceeding a flagged hourly threshold highlighted for a second look before it goes out.
Once approved, invoices send automatically to clients by email with a secure payment link, and unpaid invoices past 15 days automatically trigger a polite follow-up reminder.

What used to take the billing manager a day and a half of manual compiling each month now takes under an hour of review, and invoices consistently go out on the same date every cycle instead of drifting later each month.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a billing manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time.
tools: Practice management/billing software (e.g., Clio or TimeSolv)

automations.title: New Matter Conflict Check Automation
automations.summary: The instant a new matter is entered into the intake system through a Jotform submission or directly in Clio Grow, the automation automatically…
steps: The instant a new matter is entered into the intake system through a Jotform submission or directly in Clio Grow, the automation automatically cross-references every party name, opposing party, and related entity against the firm's existing and former client database before the matter can move forward to formal acceptance.

Any potential match automatically routes to conflicts counsel through a Slack alert with the matching records attached for manual review, and the new matter is held in a "pending conflict check" status in the practice management system until it's cleared.
Clean checks automatically clear the matter to proceed to engagement letter generation without any manual gatekeeping step.

Running a conflict check on every single matter automatically, instead of relying on someone to remember to run it before accepting a new client, closes off one of the more common and costly compliance gaps at growing firms.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a conflicts counsel, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Web form tool (e.g., Jotform or Gravity Forms)

automations.title: Client Portal Activity Alert System
automations.summary: The moment a client uploads a document or sends a message through the firm's secure client portal in Clio or NetDocuments, the automation…
steps: The moment a client uploads a document or sends a message through the firm's secure client portal in Clio or NetDocuments, the automation automatically notifies the assigned attorney and the practice administrator through Slack, tagging the alert with the client's name and matter number so it's immediately clear which file needs attention.

Messages left unread for more than four business hours automatically escalate with a second reminder, and any upload flagged as urgent by the client triggers an immediate text through Twilio rather than waiting for the next email check.
A running Google Sheets log tracks response times across the whole team so the practice administrator can spot which matters are falling behind on portal responsiveness.
Nothing a client submits through the portal sits unread overnight anymore, and firms running this typically cut portal response time from the better part of a day down to a few hours.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a practice administrator has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Secure client portal (e.g., Clio's client portal or NetDocuments)

automations.title: Settlement Disbursement Checklist Automation
automations.summary: Once a settlement is marked approved in Clio, the automation automatically generates a disbursement checklist specific to that matter type, covering…
steps: Once a settlement is marked approved in Clio, the automation automatically generates a disbursement checklist specific to that matter type, covering attorney fees, outstanding case costs, medical liens, and the client's net proceeds, and assigns each line item as a task to the settlement coordinator and accounting.

A Zapier workflow notifies the accounting team in QuickBooks Online immediately so funds can be processed against a documented checklist instead of someone reconstructing the disbursement from scratch for each settlement.
The client automatically receives a plain-language disbursement summary once every line item is marked complete, along with an estimated timeline for their check.

Because every settlement follows the same automated checklist, disbursement errors, a missed lien or a miscalculated fee, drop sharply, and settlements that used to take a week to fully process often clear within two or three business days.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a settlement coordinator remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Practice management software (e.g., Clio or MyCase)

automations.title: Non-Converted Consultation Nurture Sequence
automations.summary: When a prospect completes a paid or free consultation in Clio Grow but doesn't sign an engagement letter within a set window, the automation…
steps: When a prospect completes a paid or free consultation in Clio Grow but doesn't sign an engagement letter within a set window, the automation automatically enrolls them in a long-term nurture sequence in ActiveCampaign built around their specific practice area rather than letting the lead go cold.

The sequence mixes educational content, relevant case results, and periodic soft check-in emails spaced out over several months, and any prospect who clicks back into pricing or scheduling content automatically gets flagged to the business development coordinator for a personal follow-up call.
